To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GnRH analogs buserelin and fertirelin are equally efficacious in managing particularly stubborn cystic ovarian follicles in dairy cows.
a single injection of either 200 microg of fertirelin or 20 microg of buserelin was equally effective in inducing luteinization in follicular cystic dairy cows.
a single injection of either 200 microg of fertirelin or 20 microg of buserelin was equally effective in managing follicular cysts in lactating dairy cows.

the application of the GnRH agonist, fertirelin, for the treatment of persistent follicular cysts, and its comparison with buserelin.
the application of GnRH analogs to dairy cows with follicular cysts and with the use of milk progesterone as a diagnostic aid in this regard.
the application of a GnRH analog, fertirelin, in the treatment of ovarian follicular cyst in dairy cows.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GnRH analogs are effective in managing follicular cysts in dairy cows, and that the treatment-to-conception interval is similar to that of the normal cow.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a single injection of either analog is effective for the management of follicular cysts, and that progesterone profiles spanning at least 15 d are more accurate than the conventional 2-d profiles for the diagnosis of cystic cows.
the use of skim milk progesterones for differential diagnosis of ovarian follicular cyst is more accurate than that based on rectal palpation alone.
